hints: Write the volume formula for a cube: $V = x^3$.
Differentiate with respect to $x$: $\frac{dV}{dx} = 3x^2$, and evaluate at $x = 20$.
Use the chain rule $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dx} \times \frac{dx}{dt}$ with $\frac{dx}{dt} = 0.01\text{ cm min}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Write the volume of the cube in terms of edge length $x$ and differentiate:
$$V = x^3 \implies \frac{dV}{dx} = 3x^2$$

Evaluate the rate of change of volume with respect to edge length at $x = 20\text{ cm}$:
$$\left.\frac{dV}{dx}\right|_{x=20} = 3(20^2) = 3(400) = 1200\text{ cm}^2$$

Apply the chain rule to find $\frac{dV}{dt}$ using $\frac{dx}{dt} = 0.01\text{ cm min}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} = 1200 \times 0.01 = 12\text{ cm}^3\text{min}^{-1}$$
